title: Mandarin/Pineapple Orange Salad
status: Complete editorial review; implemented and production verified

exactBefore.body:
## Chef's Note

Citrus salads are a Southern and Caribbean tradition - canned or fresh fruit with a bright dressing and sometimes nuts for crunch. The trick is draining fruit well so the salad doesn't turn watery. If you're using canned fruit, rinse it under cold water to remove the heavy syrup, then dress it right before serving.

## Directions

1.  **Dissolve:** In a large bowl, whisk the Orange Jello and sugar into the boiling water until no crystals remain.
2.  **Emulsify:** Add the sour cream to the hot liquid. Whisk vigorously until the mixture is completely smooth and pale orange.
3.  **Texture:** Fold in the crushed pineapple (with its juice) and the drained mandarin oranges.
4.  **The Finish:** Pour the mixture into a glass bowl or a decorative mold.
5.  **Chill:** Refrigerate for **at least 4 hours** (ideally overnight) until perfectly congealed and firm.
6.  **Serve:** Serve chilled as a bright side dish or a light dessert.

frontmatter.title: Mandarin/Pineapple Orange Salad
ingredients: 1 package (3 oz) regular orange gelatin dessert mix
1 can (8 oz) canned crushed pineapple in juice, undrained; include all fruit and juice
1 can (11 oz) canned mandarin oranges, drained; discard the packing liquid

learning.focus: Dissolve the flavored gelatin completely and set a creamy fruit mixture cold.
learning.outcome: A sweet orange gelatin salad with sour cream, crushed pineapple and mandarin segments, served by the spoonful.
before: Use regular gelatin dessert mix at the displayed package size, not sugar-free mix or a vegetarian gelling product.
Use canned crushed pineapple in juice and include its juice; drain the mandarin packing liquid. Keep the sour cream cold until mixing.
Choose a shallow serving bowl with headroom; larger amounts need separate complete dishes rather than a deep bowl with an unchanged chill clock.

checkpoints.cue: There are no undissolved gelatin or sugar grains.
checkpoints.why: A smooth dissolved base prevents gritty pockets; two minutes is a stirring check, not permission to leave grains.

checkpoints.cue: The fluid gelatin is no longer steaming and the sour cream blends evenly.
checkpoints.why: Tempering helps the cool cream incorporate into the gelatin without lumps.

checkpoints.cue: The chilled center jiggles softly without a pool of freely flowing liquid.
checkpoints.why: Fruit moisture and dish depth affect setting; a fixed four-hour clock does not guarantee the center is ready.

troubleshooting.cause: It needs more chilling, the dish is deep, or the ingredient specifications changed.
troubleshooting.fix: Continue refrigeration. For the next batch use the listed regular mix and canned fruit states; do not add more liquid or substitute sugar-free mix by box count.

troubleshooting.cause: The dissolved base and sour cream were combined with a large temperature difference.
troubleshooting.fix: Temper the cream into a still-fluid, no-longer-steaming base and whisk gently until evenly blended before folding in fruit.

learning.timing: The listed batch plans eight side portions; volume has not been measured. Allow about 15–20 minutes to dissolve and assemble, then roughly 4–6 hours or overnight to set. Dish depth and refrigerator conditions can extend chilling. Scale whole ingredient quantities together, retain each can’s fixed net size, and choose enough shallow dishes; chilling time does not multiply arithmetically.
learning.storage: Keep covered at 40°F / 4°C or below and use within 3–4 days of preparation, following any earlier deadline from the sour cream or thawed fruit. Keep total preparation and serving time out of refrigeration within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C; use ice or an insulated cooler to maintain cold holding at a gathering. Do not freeze to speed setting; freezing can damage the gel texture.

exactAfter.body:
## Chef's Note

The Gwock family’s orange gelatin salad brings crushed pineapple, mandarin oranges and a generous sour-cream finish to the holiday or potluck table. Keep the pineapple juice in this version and drain the mandarin packing liquid. Serve it chilled by the spoonful, allowing the center to set fully before bringing it to the table.

## Directions

1. **Prepare for cold holding:** Clear refrigerator space for a shallow 2-quart serving dish or bowl with room for the complete salad and some headroom. Chill the sour cream until needed. Clean the can lids before opening; drain canned mandarin oranges, keeping the pineapple juice with its fruit. Keep the fruit covered and cold until mixing.
2. **Dissolve the gelatin and sugar:** Combine regular orange gelatin dessert mix, granulated sugar, and boiling water in a heatproof mixing bowl. Stir for about 2 minutes and continue until no dry grains remain. Do not add the plain-gelatin package’s separate cold-water amount; this family route uses fruit, juice and sour cream instead.
3. **Whisk in the sour cream:** Let the dissolved mixture lose its steaming heat while still fluid. Whisk a few spoonfuls of full-fat sour cream into the still-fluid gelatin base, then gradually whisk in the remaining sour cream until evenly blended.
4. **Fold in both fruits:** Fold in canned crushed pineapple in juice and canned mandarin oranges gently, including all the pineapple juice and keeping the orange segments as intact as practical. Pour the complete mixture into the prepared serving dish; do not discard fruit or cream to make it fit.
5. **Chill until set:** Cover and refrigerate at 40°F / 4°C or below promptly. Allow about 4–6 hours or overnight, continuing until the center holds a soft jiggle with no freely sloshing liquid. Serve cold from the bowl rather than relying on a clean unmold. If the center is still loose, continue chilling.

## Cooking Notes

Use canned pineapple for this gelatin mixture; raw pineapple can interfere with setting. The full added sugar and sour cream are part of its sweet, creamy character. Keep it refrigerated until serving.

Manufacturer plain 3-oz gelatin uses 1 cup boiling plus 1 cup cold water. This family salad keeps its distinct 1-cup-boiling fruit/cream route; the manufacturer’s plain yield and extra water are not imported.
The manufacturer’s cream-cheese salad has a different formula; only the complete canned-pineapple/dairy gelatin technique is relevant.
